title: Abdominal Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a 29-year-old who presents with alternating diarrhea and constipation, abdominal pain relieved by defecation, and bloating — meeting Rome IV criteria for IBS (recurrent abdominal pain + ≥2 of: improvement with defecation, change in stool frequency, change in stool appearance). ESR and CRP are normal, ruling out inflammatory bowel disease. Stool studies are negative for infectious etiology. IBS is a diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out celiac disease (anti-tTG, anti-endomysial antibodies), C. difficile, parasites, and colorectal cancer. Conservative management is key: high-fiber diet, lactose-free trial, exercise, trigger food avoidance. Loperamide PRN for diarrhea, antispasmodics (dicyclomine/hyoscyamine) PRN. Colonoscopy/sigmoidoscopy is NOT appropriate — invasive testing loses points in stable patients with normal screening labs. TCA/SSRI for refractory cases at follow-up.

decoys.label: Colonoscopy / Sigmoidoscopy
decoys.reason_wrong: Invasive testing inappropriate in 29yo with normal labs and no alarm symptoms (IDA, weight loss, bleeding). Treat conservatively. Endoscopy/EGD also loses points.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Recurrent abdominal pain + ≥2: improvement with defecation, change in stool frequency, change in stool appearance. Normal ESR/CRP rules out IBD.

teach_me_steps.order: Rule out mimics: celiac, C. diff, parasites, IBD
teach_me_steps.reasoning: IBS is diagnosis of exclusion. Celiac serology, stool studies, inflammatory markers. Colonoscopy only if alarm features present.
Diet modification (high fiber, lactose-free trial), exercise, trigger food exclusion. Loperamide PRN. Antispasmodics PRN. Avoid invasive testing.

case_summary: IBS diagnosis of exclusion in 29yo. Rome IV criteria met. Normal ESR/CRP, no alarm symptoms. Conservative management: diet + exercise + loperamide PRN. Avoid colonoscopy.
